lead: Benue police said 46 people were arrested over the attack on Peter Obi's convoy, and Obi said he would keep the floating naira if elected. Students will get 100MB of free daily data for learning sites from 1 October, and NERC told distribution companies to put most of their operating funds into investment from 2027. The Falconets drew 0-0 with China, and the cash transfer office rejected the Auditor-General's finding on N33.75 billion.

items.h: Police arrest 46 over attack on Obi's convoy in Benue
items.s: Benue police said 46 people were arrested in connection with the attack and blockade of Peter Obi's convoy on the Gboko-Makurdi road.

items.h: Obi says he would keep the floating naira
items.s: Peter Obi named the floating of the naira as the one Tinubu policy he would retain, saying he would raise productivity to strengthen the currency. He described 2027 as a contest between Nigerians and the APC government.

items.h: Students to get 100MB free data daily from 1 October
items.s: The Federal Government said students will receive 100MB of free data each day to reach selected educational websites and learning platforms from 1 October 2026.

items.h: NERC orders DisCos to put 60% of operating funds into investment
items.s: From 2027, electricity distribution companies must allocate up to 60 per cent of their non-administrative operating expenditure to capital projects, the regulator said.

items.h: Cash transfer office rejects audit claim over N33.75bn
items.s: The National Cash Transfer Office denied the Auditor-General's finding that it lacked evidence the N33.75 billion in transfers reached beneficiaries, and said it had presented proof.

items.h: Falconets hold China to goalless draw
items.s: Nigeria's under-20 women drew 0-0 with China in Group F, keeping alive slim hopes of reaching the World Cup knockout stage.

items.h: Tinubu says he has kept his promises to national teams
items.s: President Tinubu said he has fulfilled pledges made to the Super Eagles, Super Falcons and D'Tigress after their performances in recent competitions.

items.h: Dangote says IPO will make fuel buyers refinery shareholders
items.s: Aliko Dangote said the share sale is designed so ordinary Nigerians can own part of the refinery. The independent marketers' association backed the IPO and asked for wider direct petrol allocation.

items.h: HURIWA condemns killing of Kano social media commentator
items.s: The Human Rights Writers Association condemned the reported killing of Kano political commentator Ibrahim Khalil Dan Shagamu, who had raised alarm over death threats.

items.h: NAICOM denies N100bn recapitalisation fraud claim
items.s: The insurance regulator dismissed a report alleging a N100 billion fraud in its recapitalisation exercise and the EFCC detention of its officials.

items.h: Police arrest woman over fake OPay shutdown document
items.s: The National Cybercrime Centre arrested 27-year-old Hafsat Abubakar over a forged document falsely claiming OPay was shutting down.

items.h: INEC plans polling centres for displaced people in Plateau
items.s: INEC will set up voting centres for internally displaced persons in nine local government areas of Plateau for 2027.

items.h: Court orders INEC to approve NDC's new logo
items.s: A court directed INEC to approve and upload the Nigeria Democratic Congress's modified logo for all elections.

items.h: Police and ADC supporters clash in Kaduna as campaigns begin
items.s: The ADC said its members were attacked during a walk in Kaduna and accused the APC government of deploying thugs. Police cited traffic and security concerns.

items.h: Atiku questions new borrowing and says higher allocations have not helped
items.s: Atiku Abubakar criticised a proposed Vienna-listed bond, and said larger FAAC allocations have brought more naira with less value and rising debt.

items.h: Titi Abubakar says nothing is working under Tinubu
items.s: Atiku Abubakar's wife Titi said she wonders how Nigerians are feeding given the cost of living.

items.h: Alake says Nigeria needs Tinubu beyond 2027
items.s: Solid Minerals Minister Dele Alake, a campaign spokesman, said the President's reforms need continuity.

items.h: Yari says APC will campaign on Tinubu's record
items.s: APC campaign director-general Abdulaziz Yari said the 2027 campaign will rest on performance rather than new promises or personal attacks.

items.h: SDP targets presidency and 28 states
items.s: The Social Democratic Party activated its structures nationwide at its convention in Abuja.

items.h: PDP launches Ogun governorship campaign in the rain
items.s: Supporters of PDP candidate Oladipupo Adebutu filled Abeokuta despite heavy rain as the party opened its campaign.

items.h: Ogun APC aspirant rejects primary that picked Adeola
items.s: Governorship aspirant Abayomi Hunye said the primary won by Senator Solomon Adeola was unfair and cannot stand.

items.h: Charismatic bishops back Tinubu's second term
items.s: The Charismatic Bishops Conference of Nigeria pledged support for President Tinubu's 2027 bid.

items.h: Sokoto police warn parties over electoral violence
items.s: Sokoto police commissioner Hayatu Shafa said party leaders will be held accountable for breaches of the peace by their supporters.

items.h: Lawyer warns of rising political intolerance
items.s: Human rights lawyer Monday Ubani warned politicians against threats and intimidation ahead of 2027.

items.h: Ondo investigates deaths of 24 after local drinks
items.s: The Ondo government opened an investigation into the deaths of at least 24 people in Odigbo who reportedly drank locally brewed drinks.

items.h: Floods sweep away children in Abuja and Abia
items.s: Divers joined the search for 13-year-old Alhassan Jamil, swept away by floodwater in Gwagwalada, while a girl was also lost to flooding in Abia.

items.h: Lagos electricity regulator licenses Elektron Energy to generate power
items.s: The Lagos State Electricity Regulatory Commission issued Elektron Energy a licence to generate electricity in the state.

items.h: Nigeria seeks Chinese partners to speed up power projects
items.s: The government is expanding partnerships with Chinese firms and lenders to deliver Presidential Power Initiative projects faster.

items.h: Committee formed to roll out electric buses for civil servants
items.s: The Head of the Civil Service inaugurated a nine-member committee for a pilot mass transit bus scheme for federal workers.

items.h: NCC moves to block unregistered SIM devices
items.s: The Nigerian Communications Commission began stepping up enforcement of type approval rules to keep unapproved SIM-enabled devices off networks.

items.h: NFIU launches anti-money-laundering partnership with banks and fintechs
items.s: The Nigerian Financial Intelligence Unit asked financial firms to share intelligence under a new public-private framework.

items.h: Commodity exchange launches price guarantee for 500,000 farmers
items.s: The Nigerian Commodity Exchange, Bank of Agriculture and farmers' association started a guaranteed minimum price programme.

items.h: EU and EIB invest €108m in African entrepreneurs
items.s: The EU and European Investment Bank mobilised over €500 million for African businesses, with Nigeria a major beneficiary.

items.h: FRSC launches campaign against vehicle overloading
items.s: The Federal Road Safety Corps launched a national movement for safe loading at a policy dialogue in Abuja.

items.h: Bauchi governor orders faster work on erosion project
items.s: Governor Bala Mohammed told the contractor on a 15.2km ACReSAL flood and erosion project to add equipment and staff.

items.h: Kano police arrest fake officer over recruitment fraud
items.s: Kano police arrested 35-year-old Adamu Musa for allegedly posing as a chief superintendent and defrauding people.

items.h: Mastercard and Busha simplify crypto transfers in Nigeria
items.s: Busha users can now send and receive supported digital assets using an email or phone number through Mastercard Crypto Credential.

items.h: Trump promises $5,000 to Americans if Republicans keep Congress
items.s: US President Donald Trump pledged a $5,000 payment to every adult if his party retains control in November.

items.h: Algeria cuts ties with the UAE
items.s: Algeria severed diplomatic relations with the United Arab Emirates over actions it called hostile.

items.h: Canada lets foreign workers study without permits
items.s: Eligible foreign workers in Canada may now take courses of up to six months without a study permit.
